name: Zulu Kingdom

areaKm2.note: world_1878 polygon "Zululand" = 25,400 km2 on the sphere (Thukela to Phongolo); kingdom with its northern marches ~27,000-32,000 km2.

population.note: Page infobox: 250,000 in 1828. Estimates for Cetshwayo's kingdom in 1879 run ~250,000-400,000 (Laband, Kingdom in Crisis ch. 1); no census.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: no towns; royal amakhanda (military homesteads) of a few thousand people each.

activePersonnel.note: Page infobox: 35,000-60,000 Zulu (Colenso 1880 p. 318: army 35,000, 4,000 kept with Cetshwayo). The amabutho were assembled at oNdini in January 1879, so the army counts as under arms. About 20,000-25,000 at Isandlwana (battle page).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: older married amabutho and local levies not called to oNdini.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: izindibi carrier boys and royal attendants.

mobilizationRatio.note: Every man was enrolled in an age-set ibutho; 35,000-60,000 warriors (Anglo-Zulu War page) of 250,000-400,000 people = 14-20%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Close-order amabutho fighting in the horns-of-the-buffalo formation with isijula/iklwa spears and cowhide shields; total army less skirmishers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25 or below. Evidence: stabbing spears and shields against Martini-Henry rifles and artillery, several generations behind

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: lifelong age-set regiments, fast cross-country movement

count.note: Educated guess: warriors with firearms (~20,000 old muskets and some rifles in the kingdom) used as skirmishers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: obsolete trade muskets, little ammunition

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: poor marksmanship

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Ntshingwayo kaMahole's envelopment at Isandlwana; Cetshwayo's defensive strategy

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: age-set regimental identity; charged into rifle and Gatling fire at Kambula and Ulundi

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: defence of the homeland against invasion

weapons.note: Anchor: 3 (iron weapons). Evidence: iron stabbing spears and throwing spears, a few muskets

armor.note: Anchor: 1 (leather). Evidence: cowhide isihlangu shields, no armour

ships.note: Anchor: 0 (rafts, canoes). Evidence: no watercraft of military use

fortification.note: Anchor: 0 (palisade). Evidence: stockaded homesteads, caves and the Hlobane strongholds

logistics.note: Anchor: 0 (porters). Evidence: boy carriers and cattle driven with the impi, 3-4 days' food

isr.note: Anchor: 0-1 (runners). Evidence: excellent scouts and spies, but foot messengers only

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess: cattle-keeping and hoe-agriculture society near subsistence; Maddison has no estimate (South Africa 1879 = 1,985 reflects the colonial economy and is not comparable).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: amabutho served the king as unpaid labour and soldiers; not a monetary budget.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: iron smelting and smithing only.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: cattle herds and royal grain stores fed the assembled army for days only.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. A new ibutho was formed every few years from youths of the same age.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: no engineered roads; wagon tracks made by traders and the British.

railKm.note: Educated guess: no railway in Zululand (Natal had ~110 km in 1879).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: no port; the coast was open beach.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: impis carried a few days' food and drove cattle.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: no wheeled transport; cattle were food, not draught animals.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row plus full population support; no fortified cities, so below the full 1.2 row.

notes: Snapshot = Zulu Kingdom in January 1879 when the British invasion began. Territory and population = Cetshwayo's kingdom between the Thukela and the Phongolo; includes is empty. Personnel: the whole assembled amabutho = active (they were mustered at oNdini for the first-fruits ceremony and the war); older regiments not called = trainedReserves. Army size from the Anglo-Zulu War page (Colenso 1880; 35,000-60,000) and Isandlwana page (20,000-25,000 engaged). Economy and logistics values are educated guesses: no statistics exist for the kingdom. Tech levels sit far below the industrial anchors by design.
